L36: "Sáu bước trên luôn xảy ra, kể cả khi không ai gọi tên chúng." Lesson attributes it to "The team's note" (section 4), not to a standard.
Loop framing is supported by the file's own trip: L31-32 "Đội phát hiện thêm một lỗi ... Lỗi này quay lại bước 1." Presented as the lesson's reading, consistent with the source.

L37-38: "làm cả sáu bước cho một tính năng nhỏ trong hai tuần, hay làm cả sáu bước cho cả hệ thống trong một năm." Supports "in weeks" vs "a year". Lesson's "in a week or two" is looser than the file's "hai tuần" but not contradicted.

L39: "Vòng nhỏ không tạo ra ít tài liệu hơn; nó làm cho việc sai sớm rẻ hơn." The lesson's "shorter distance between a decision and the evidence" is an interpretation consistent with "sai sớm rẻ hơn".

L22 says the criteria were "được viết trước khi code" (written before the code), passive, no author. "agreed" and "somebody else's agreement" add an agreeing party the file does not name; section 5 itself says "The file does not say who wrote them".
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Because the conditions were written before the code, the tester re-runs something that already existed instead of deciding what correct means; the same step also finds cases those conditions missed.

claim_verdicts.evidence: "On many teams you also check each agreed condition yourself" is a general-practice statement; no docs root in versions.yaml covers it and the repo file gives step 4 only to "Tester" (L22). Hedged in sections 5 and 9; unhedged in section 7 (see issue). Kind opinion, non-blocking.

issues.text: Carried over from previous round, not applied. "Expected result" states step 4 as shared without the hedge used in sections 5, 9 and the suggested answer ("on many teams"/"often"); the file gives step 4 to "Tester" alone (L22).

issues.text: Carried over, not applied. "entirely yours" overstates step 3: the file's step 3 has two builders, "Một người làm phần API, một người làm phần giao diện" (L17); section 5 of the lesson itself says "two people on separate branches".

issues.text: Section 4 told me the one line I was handed is the output of step 1. Here it is the output of two earlier steps. I stopped to work out that the task must also carry step 2's scope decision.
issues.quote: Actually the line you were handed is the output of two earlier steps and the input to three later ones
issues.fix: Replace "the line you were handed" with "the task you were handed, its one line plus the team's scope decision," so it matches section 4's "output of step 1".

issues.text: Sections 4 and 5 never say who releases (step 5) or who operates (step 6); only misconception 3 asserts later steps are settled by somebody else. The Try-it expected result and summary line 5 rely on that, so I had to borrow it from the misconception to decide steps 5-6 were not mine.
issues.quote: steps 5 and 6 from whoever on your team releases and watches the system
issues.fix: In section 4, add to "Step 5 puts it in front of users." the words "usually done by whoever on the team releases and watches the system, not by the builder".

issues.text: Section 2 says my first task is this feature and the repository has no application. Section 5 says the team already took this same feature around the loop. I briefly could not tell whether the feature exists or I am building it.
issues.quote: The team's note records how they already took this same feature around the loop, in Vietnamese; picture yourself as its builder.
issues.fix: Add one clause: "the note is a worked example written for this lesson, not code in the repository; picture yourself as its builder."

issues.text: I re-read this twice: why does narrowing the scope make a decision worth writing down? The link between the two halves is not stated.
issues.quote: It is written down because it narrows the scope — the set of orders the feature must handle — so much.
issues.fix: Add the missing link: "It is written down because it narrows the scope ... so much that anyone who did not hear it would build the wrong thing."

issues.text: "their own daily" first parsed as a noun ("their own daily [thing]"); I re-read the sentence.
issues.quote: each merging the main branch into their own daily
issues.fix: Write "each merging the main branch into their own branch every day".

issues.text: Option d: step 6 is what "the team learned"; I am on the team, so I hesitated whether the measurement counts as "somebody else rather than you". I ticked it using the Try-it answer, not the body.
issues.quote: Which of these were produced by somebody else rather than by you?
issues.fix: Reword the stem to "Which of these came from somebody else or from the whole team, rather than from your own step?" (en and vi).

issues.text: Option a restates the Core concepts line on the cost of being wrong almost word for word, so I can pick it by matching wording rather than by reasoning about trip size.
issues.quote: The cost is the work built on top of the decision before anyone noticed, and a small trip meets real users while little has been built.
issues.fix: Reword option a in terms of the example: "On a small trip, the refunds rule meets customers after two weeks of building on it, not a year." (en and vi).

issues.text: Correct option c echoes misconception 1's phrase "shortens the wait for feedback", so it can be picked by recognising the phrase.
issues.quote: only the wait for feedback got shorter
issues.fix: Rephrase c's tail to "what changed was how soon the decisions met real users" (en and vi).
